stem: For a school project, Meera compares two planets. Planet X is closer to the Sun than planet Y, and both have similar thick atmospheres that trap heat in the same way. Which statement correctly predicts their general temperatures?

options.text: Planet Y must be hotter because it is farther from the Sun.
Planet X is generally hotter because it receives more energy from the Sun.
Both planets must have exactly the same temperature because their atmospheres are similar.
The temperatures cannot be predicted at all, even when the atmospheres are similar.

teacher.key_rationale: With comparable atmospheres, the nearer planet receives more solar energy and is generally hotter, so B is correct. Option A is the trap for a student who reverses the distance-temperature relationship; C ignores the role of distance; D overstates the atmosphere's effect by claiming prediction is impossible.
